holidays.name: National Eat What You Want Day
holidays.description: A glorious day when you are encouraged to ditch the diet, ignore the nutrition label, and eat whatever your heart desires, whether that is cake for breakfast or a bowl of pickles for dessert.
holidays.origin: Created in the 1990s by author and food enthusiast Thomas and Ruth Roy, who also founded many other quirky food days. It was designed as a guilt-free break from calorie counting.
holidays.funFact: Many people who celebrate it report that the most popular choice is dessert first, proving that the inner child never really leaves the dinner table.

holidays.name: National Foster Care Day
holidays.description: Not to be confused with a silly day, this one is a heartfelt observance, but it is often celebrated with unconventional events like pet-fostering drives where people temporarily adopt animals for a good cause.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States around mid-May to raise awareness for children and animals who need temporary homes, linking with broader foster care awareness campaigns.
holidays.funFact: Fostering a single shelter pet frees up a kennel space that can help save another animal's life, so one couch can rescue two pets.

holidays.name: Twilight Zone Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of eerie twists, spooky narrators, and stories that end with a shocking surprise. Fans marathon classic episodes and speak in dramatic, ominous voices for no reason at all.
holidays.origin: Celebrates the anniversary of Rod Serling's iconic anthology series, which first aired on CBS in the late 1950s and became a pillar of science fiction and horror television.
holidays.funFact: Rod Serling wrote about 92 of the 156 episodes of the original series, meaning he personally created most of the weirdness himself.

holidays.name: Eat What You Want Day Companion: Mother's Day Eve Pajama Brunch
holidays.description: An unofficial tradition in which people hold a lazy brunch in pajamas, complete with absurdly oversized pancakes, in honor of the unsung heroes who have to wash all the syrup off the dishes.
holidays.origin: Grew out of social media trends in which families share breakfast-in-bed photos around the second weekend of May, turning a sentimental custom into a viral pajama party.
holidays.funFact: Breakfast in bed is statistically one of the most commonly attempted and most commonly messy gifts of the year, with burnt toast leading the disaster charts.

holidays.name: Limerick Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate five-line, bouncy, and often cheeky poems with a strict AABBA rhyme scheme. Participants are encouraged to write their own silly verses and read them aloud with dramatic flair.
holidays.origin: Observed on May 12 in honor of the birthday of Edward Lear, the English poet who popularized the form, but many enthusiasts start the festivities a day early on May 11 to warm up their rhyming muscles.
holidays.funFact: Despite the name, the limerick has no confirmed link to the Irish city of Limerick, and historians still argue over how it got its name.
